messages.subject: A pcount framework question
parts:
Dear list members,

I hope my question is not out of the range of questions for the list.
One of my students is sampling bats with mist-nets and we are trying to analyze the data with the pcount framework (individuals were not marked).  Is it a reasonable approach? What will be the interpretation of the results?  It could be interpreted as an index of abundance as average number of bats per mistnet/hours?

Any help would be appreciated,

Manuel

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] A pcount framework question
parts:
hi Manuel,

 I think it is reasonable to view y[i,t] = # bats caught during sample t at net i as a binomial count. Therefore it seems reasonable to use the N-mixture model.   I'm guessing the capture rate of bats is extremely low and therefore the model parameters might be poorly identified. Conceptually though N would be the size of some population of exposed bats.

 Can you mark these bats somehow?

regards,
andy

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] A pcount framework question
parts:
Hello,

I would like to revive this question as I have a similar approach I'd like to try. I would like to estimate the probability of detection/capture of different sex/ages of birds in an array of 12-16 mist nets at different locations.Similar to a count methodology, I will have two consecutive occasions for netting at each site.

Could I build a model, like Manuel with N-mixture or occu for each species' sex separately? With this approach, these nets would not be more than 30-50 meters apart from each other, would there be issues of independence with this? Should I pool the observations per site instead to get a site probability of capture?

Any ideas or tips would be very helpful. I would like to account for differences in captures between the sexes to build other models.

Thanks

Fabiola Rodríguez
